acceptance: New Snowflake bundles record the size actually used (observed after any resize) in config.warehouse_size; a requested size that was not applied is not recorded as the size used. A test covers modify_warehouse_settings false and true.

Every published Snowflake bundle whose config.warehouse_size differs from its recorded observed size is corrected to the observed size, through the repository's sanctioned corpus-correction path (sidecar or correction record if one exists; otherwise a reviewed bundle edit with a CORPUS_NOTES entry). Owner authorizes correcting these published bundles.
validate_corpus passes; the site inputs and explorer show the corrected size after republish; the PR lists every corrected bundle.
context: Owner decision 2026-11-18: 'new bundles record the real warehouse size used. existing bundles are corrected with the real size used.' Evidence: platform.compute.warehouse_size X-Small observed in all 50; config MEDIUM is the unapplied default. Guardrails: no live-cloud runs; linked worktree; changelog fragment; any integrity hash or signature over bundles must be handled by the repo's own tooling, never hand-patched.
description:
Problem: all 50 published Snowflake bundles record config.warehouse_size MEDIUM while platform.compute.warehouse_size (observed via SHOW WAREHOUSES) is X-Small. MEDIUM is the adapter default (benchbox/platforms/snowflake.py ~144) and is applied only when modify_warehouse_settings is true (~162, default False), so the warehouse was never resized.

Outcome (owner decision 2026-11-18): new bundles record the warehouse size actually used; the 50 existing bundles are corrected to the real size used.
